catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Extraction focused on cas_runner, agent governance, skills specification, and flow execution pipelines.
analysis_limits: Dynamic runtime evaluation of remote LLM calls was not conducted
Analysis limited to codebase tree, configuration, manifests, and declared symbols

system_map.overview: The CAS (Continuous Architecture System) runner provides an agentic execution and governance harness. It combines declarative skill specifications and CLI commands with structured flow orchestration, model abstractions via LiteLLM, and automated compliance and governance action engines.

agents.name: FlowRunner
agents.role: Orchestrates multi-step agentic workflows and manages step execution context.

agents.name: AgenticMerger
agents.role: Reconciles and merges agent-generated state, branch specs, and architectural decisions.

agents.name: GovernanceActionEngine
agents.role: Enforces state transition rules and executes governed architectural mutations.

agents.name: ComplianceEngine
agents.role: Evaluates architectural invariants and flags compliance findings across project knowledge.

orchestration.description: Centralized pipeline execution orchestrated through FlowRunner, constrained by deterministic governance engines and transition registries.

tools_and_integrations.name: LiteLLMClient
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Unified interface to query foundational LLM providers with consistent parameter mapping.

tools_and_integrations.name: MockLLMClient
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Deterministic simulation of model responses for testing agentic flows without network calls or costs.

tools_and_integrations.name: OpenTelemetry Instrumentation
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Traces agent actions and state transitions across lifecycle steps.

state_and_memory.description: File-backed architecture state, steering projections, markdown artifacts, and governance models in cas-knowledge.
Step execution context, intermediate resolution results, and runtime health scores evaluated during runs.

patterns.name: Declarative Agent Command Manifests

tool_protocols.notes: Commands specify entrypoints and task directives declaratively via TOML.

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures prompt configurations and agent skills are version-controlled alongside application code.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Externalizes task-specific prompts and steps into reproducible declarative manifests.

patterns.summary: Agent behaviors, skills, and subcommands are declared in isolated TOML configuration files to decouple prompting from runtime harnesses.
patterns.intent: Standardize agent invocations across different lifecycle phases (plan, specify, clarify, tasks) using human-readable configuration.
patterns.context: Used in `.agents/commands/` to control speckit agent skills (e.g. speckit.plan.toml, speckit.specify.toml, speckit.tasks.toml).
forces: Need consistent command execution without hardcoding prompt strings into python source
Support rapid iteration on agent instructions without rebuilding binaries
patterns.solution: Define command goals, steps, and parameters in TOML manifests placed under `.agents/commands/` that map directly into skills directories.

evidence.note: Defines the specification agent task declaration
Defines the planning agent command manifest

benefits: Portable agent definitions that can be shared across agents and developers
Clean separation of orchestration logic from agent prompts
costs: Requires strict schema validation for TOML files to prevent runtime errors
Risk of drift between skill implementation and command definitions
failure_modes: Mismatched command parameters resulting in skill execution failure

patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt a directory-based command declaration pattern for agent capabilities rather than inline prompt construction in code.

patterns.name: Governed Action State Machine

tool_protocols.notes: Actions are mediated via TransitionRegistry before execution.

optimisation_targets.notes: Guarantees that agents cannot mutate architectural state into an invalid configuration.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Strictly constrains agent actions to registered state machine transitions.

patterns.summary: Constrains autonomous mutations by routing all candidate operations through a formal TransitionRegistry and GovernanceActionEngine.
patterns.intent: Prevent unauthorized or out-of-order state mutations proposed by LLMs or automated tools.
patterns.context: Employed in `src/cas_runner/governance/governance_action_engine.py` to gate project state updates.
forces: LLMs can generate arbitrary actions that violate domain business logic
State changes must be auditable and reproducible
patterns.solution: Define explicit state transitions in a TransitionRegistry. The GovernanceActionEngine validates candidate GovernanceAction instances against valid transitions before applying state changes.
implementation_signals: Engine checking pre-conditions and executing actions via `GovernanceActionService`

evidence.note: Registry checks valid state transitions before applying governance actions
Service layer executing validated governance actions

benefits: Ensures all agent mutations adhere to codified compliance constraints
costs: New actions require updating and validating registry transitions
Can reject valid but unprecedented agent initiatives
failure_modes: Deadlock if a required intermediate transition is unregistered or misconfigured

patterns.reuse_notes: Use a transition registry to intermediate between an agent's suggested tool actions and actual persistent state stores.

patterns.name: Agentic Merge and Conflict Resolution

tool_protocols.notes: Merger evaluates artifacts and returns a typed ResolutionResult.

optimisation_targets.notes: Synthesizes divergent agentic proposals without dropping structural integrity.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Empowers an agentic component to resolve conflicts between multiple model-generated proposals.

patterns.summary: Resolves divergent agent-generated changes and branch specifications through an automated semantic merge engine.
patterns.intent: Resolve discrepancies between parallel agent workstreams without requiring manual human git cherry-picking.
patterns.context: Found in `src/cas_runner/governance/agentic_merger.py` handling concurrent specs and artifact changes.
forces: Multiple agents or run steps can generate conflicting updates to project specifications
Simple textual 3-way git merges fail on semantic JSON/Markdown schema conflicts
patterns.solution: Encapsulate resolution in `AgenticMerger`, taking candidate artifacts and outputting a structured `ResolutionResult` with confidence and conflict markers.
implementation_signals: Return type `ResolutionResult` containing status and resolved contents

evidence.note: Performs merge logic on agent outputs
Typed contract containing outcome of merge resolution

benefits: Reduces manual intervention for non-trivial semantic conflicts
Produces structured diagnostics on conflicting elements
costs: Risk of hallucinated resolution when conflicting intents are fundamentally incompatible
Requires evaluation of LLM merge confidence
failure_modes: Silent loss of domain intent during aggressive automated reconciliation

patterns.reuse_notes: Implement semantic resolution workers that operate on typed ASTs or structured schemas rather than raw text diffs.

patterns.name: Dual-Client LLM Provider Abstraction

tool_protocols.notes: Wraps LiteLLM to normalize LLM requests across diverse backends.

optimisation_targets.notes: Enables deterministic unit testing and provider independence.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Hides provider-specific quirks behind a standardized interface.

patterns.summary: Decouples agent core logic from specific model providers by pairing a multi-provider gateway with a strict mock client interface.
patterns.intent: Provide swappable, observable LLM invocation with deterministic offline mocking for fast local testing.
patterns.context: Located in `src/cas_runner/llm/` supporting FlowRunner and governance engines.
forces: Agent pipelines must run in CI/CD without making expensive and non-deterministic real API calls
Production runtime requires multi-model flexibility across OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, etc.
patterns.solution: Define `LiteLLMClient` for production calls wrapping `litellm` and `MockLLMClient` implementing identical method signatures with canned or heuristic responses.
implementation_signals: Pair of classes: `LiteLLMClient` and `MockLLMClient` with matching interfaces

evidence.note: Offline test double ensuring CI determinism

benefits: Zero-cost, repeatable testing of complex agent loops
Seamless switching between model backends without touching agent workflow logic
costs: Mock client must be maintained to accurately emulate real model response structures
Can mask model-specific prompt sensitivity during unit test runs
failure_modes: Mocks drift from real provider schema changes leading to production runtime failures

patterns.reuse_notes: Always provide a mock implementation conforming to your agent system's LLM interface for robust integration and unit testing.

patterns.name: Typed Governance Data Contracts

tool_protocols.notes: Pydantic models enforce schema contracts across all state persistence points.

optimisation_targets.notes: Strict types guarantee structured communication between agents and engines.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Replaces open-ended string outputs with strictly validated domain schemas.

patterns.summary: All state transitions, metrics, health indicators, and findings are represented as strongly-typed Pydantic domain models.
patterns.intent: Eliminate unstructured string manipulation and enforce compile-time/runtime validation for agent data exchanges.
forces: Agents generate text that easily diverges from required formats
Downstream dashboards and analyzers require predictable data shapes
patterns.solution: Define comprehensive Pydantic models (ComplianceFinding, GovernanceHealth, GovernanceAction, etc.) that enforce typing, defaults, and serializability.
implementation_signals: Field validations and schema export capabilities

evidence.note: Comprehensive typed schemas governing all system metrics and action results

benefits: Runtime validation halts malformed agent outputs early
Serves as self-documenting contract for both agents and human developers
costs: Models must be kept updated when underlying domain requirements evolve
failure_modes: Validation errors thrown at runtime when LLM responses drop required fields

patterns.reuse_notes: Use Pydantic or equivalent data validation libraries to model every inter-agent and inter-step message contract.

patterns.name: Sequential Flow Runner Orchestration

optimisation_targets.notes: Simplifies execution flow and error recovery.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Linear pipeline execution is easier to reason about and trace than autonomous swarms.

patterns.summary: Executes multi-step agentic procedures sequentially with a shared execution context passed along the step chain.
patterns.intent: Coordinate step-by-step agent activities with deterministic order and context propagation.
forces: Complex agent operations (e.g. assess, plan, specify, validate) must run in strict sequence
Later steps require access to artifacts produced by earlier steps
patterns.solution: FlowRunner coordinates pipeline execution, feeding the accumulated output of preceding steps as input context to subsequent steps.

evidence.note: Main pipeline runner coordinating multi-step execution
CLI command dispatcher launching FlowRunner flows

benefits: Predictable execution paths and straightforward telemetry capture
Easy to pause, resume, or replay failed steps
costs: Cannot naturally leverage opportunistic parallel execution between independent steps
failure_modes: Single step failure blocks subsequent pipeline steps unless explicitly marked optional

patterns.reuse_notes: Use a sequential context-passing runner for developer-facing workflows where transparency and control outweigh raw autonomy.

patterns.name: Continuous Compliance Evaluator

tool_protocols.notes: Inspects project inventory against codified compliance checks.

optimisation_targets.notes: Produces actionable compliance findings for governance reviews.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Automates compliance checks while keeping findings transparent and inspectable.

patterns.summary: Regularly evaluates the system state against architectural invariants and generates structured compliance findings.
patterns.intent: Detect architectural drift, broken links, and policy violations created during agent or human modifications.
forces: Uncontrolled agent edits can slowly degrade architectural consistency
Manual audits are too slow to keep pace with rapid agentic updates
patterns.solution: Execute `ComplianceEngine` scans to evaluate rules over project manifests and generate `ComplianceFinding` entries accompanied by aggregate `ComplianceMetrics`.

evidence.note: Evaluator executing architectural rules against project state

benefits: Continuous feedback loop detecting architectural violations immediately
Quantifiable metrics for repository health tracking
costs: Rule definitions require explicit maintenance as architectural conventions change
False positives can stall deployment workflows
failure_modes: Outdated rule sets triggering alert fatigue across the development team

patterns.reuse_notes: Implement deterministic rule checkers that run after agent generation steps to catch structural issues before code review.

patterns.name: Composite Health Scoring Heuristic

tool_protocols.notes: Mathematical evaluation of metrics to determine system health.

optimisation_targets.notes: Gives clear diagnostic signals on repository health.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Uses deterministic weighting rather than opaque LLM opinion to compute project health.

patterns.summary: Computes project architecture health using weighted metrics and generates human-readable health reasons.
patterns.intent: Synthesize diverse compliance findings, risks, and inventory metrics into an interpretable status grade.
forces: Raw metrics lists are overwhelming for operators to digest quickly
LLMs need concrete feedback signals to gauge whether a change improved or damaged project health
patterns.solution: Aggregate metrics via `calculate_health` into a categorical `HealthStatus` (e.g. green, yellow, red) and extract contributing explanations with `get_health_reasons`.

evidence.note: Health calculation logic and descriptive reason extractors

benefits: Provides unambiguous go/no-go signals for automated merges and promotions
Explains the exact reasons behind degraded health scores
costs: Weights and thresholds must be calibrated to avoid over-sensitivity
May oversimplify complex architectural nuances into a single status
failure_modes: Metric gaming where agents satisfy threshold rules without addressing underlying technical debt

patterns.reuse_notes: Combine multiple discrete agent findings into a single scored health model with explainability functions for dashboards and gating.

anti_patterns.name: Unbounded Agent Action Escalation
symptoms: Agent actions executed without prior validation against `TransitionRegistry`
Direct disk or git state mutations initiated outside the `GovernanceActionService`

where_observed.note: Guards exist specifically to prevent direct, unmediated action dispatch

impact: Undetected architectural drift and broken compliance constraints
suggested_remediation: Enforce all mutations through `GovernanceActionEngine.execute` and verify valid transitions in `TransitionRegistry` before applying any state changes.

anti_patterns.name: Unmonitored Mock Divergence
symptoms: Mock client returns responses that do not reflect newer LiteLLM API versions or model token output nuances
Agent prompt regressions passing in CI but failing on live LLM endpoints

where_observed.note: Static responses in MockLLMClient can mask real-world prompt parsing failures

impact: False confidence in test suite passing while production flows break on schema mismatches
suggested_remediation: Implement periodic contract validation runs comparing live LiteLLM outputs with MockLLMClient fixture structures.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Command manifests and skill definitions externalize prompt templates into TOML files under `.agents/` rather than embedded code strings.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Decouples prompt authoring and prompt versioning from runner engine code.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: OpenTelemetry SDK and API integrated at the runner dependency level for distributed trace context propagation.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Enables end-to-end tracing across CLI commands, runner flows, and LLM calls.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Formal TransitionRegistry acts as an invariant firewall against unauthorized governance actions.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Prevents unauthorized states even when generated by autonomous agent reasoning.

open_questions.question: How are dynamic prompt variables and context variables interpolated into `.agents/commands/*.toml` manifests during runtime?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Determines whether prompt templates can suffer from prompt injection or syntax errors when combining user inputs.
open_questions.evidence_gap: Manifest parsing details in `FlowRunner` or skill runners were not fully inspectable from the manifest list alone.
